chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Sadaqa, from Salih al-Nayli, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who visits the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), recognizing his right, Allah will write for him the reward of freeing a thousand slaves, and [reward him] like the one who rides out with a thousand saddled and bridled horses in the way of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to emphasize that the spiritual merit of Ziyarah to Imam Al-Husayn (as) is contingent upon 'Ma'rifah' (gnostic recognition) of his divine station, not merely physical presence. This comparison to freeing a thousand slaves or equipping a thousand horses for jihad underscores the immense weight of his sacrifice in Shia theology, linking the act of visitation directly to the redemption and merit of the Ahl al-Bayt's struggle.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Muhammad Bin Sadaqa, from Salih Al Nayli who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who goes to the grave of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> recognising his<sup>asws</sup> right, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him the Recompense of freeing a thousand people, and he would be like the one who readies a thousand horses with saddles and reins in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn has narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Muhammad ibn Sadaqah from Salih al-Niliy who has said the following:

“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, Tor one who visits the grave of al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, with proper understanding of his rights, Allah writes for him the reward for setting free of one thousand persons. It is like readying one thousand horses fully harnessed to join the battle for the cause of Allah.”’
